name: Swiss Bircher muesli
steps: Stir the oats, yogurt and milk together in a bowl or jar until no dry oats remain.
Coarsely grate the apple, skin on, straight into the bowl and stir it through with a squeeze of lemon so it stays pale.
Cover and leave in the fridge for at least 10 minutes, or overnight for a softer, creamier texture.
Toast the chopped hazelnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until fragrant, then let them cool.
Loosen the muesli with a splash of milk if it has thickened, then top with the hazelnuts and drizzle with honey.
tip: Make three jars on Sunday evening; they keep for 3 days in the fridge, and adding the apple fresh each morning keeps it crisp.

name: Peanut butter overnight oats
steps: Whisk the whey into the milk in a jar until there are no lumps, then stir in the oats.
Spoon the peanut butter on top and swirl it lightly through with a knife so you get ribbons rather than a uniform mix.
Close the jar and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
In the morning stir, add a splash more milk if it is too thick, and top with the sliced banana just before eating.
tip: Swap the whey for a plant protein and the milk for soy drink to make it dairy-free; it keeps for 2 days in a sealed jar.

name: Vegan berry overnight oats
steps: Shake the pea protein and soy drink together in a lidded jar for 15 seconds until smooth.
Add the oats, chia seeds and maple syrup and stir well, scraping the bottom so the chia does not clump.
Tip the frozen berries on top; they will thaw overnight and release their juice into the oats.
Refrigerate for at least 6 hours, then stir once more and eat cold or microwave for 90 seconds if you prefer it warm.
tip: Use certified gluten-free oats if you need it gluten-free; the jars keep 3 days in the fridge.

name: Protein porridge
steps: Put the oats and milk in a small saucepan with a pinch of salt and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until the oats are soft and the porridge coats the spoon.
Take the pan off the heat and let it stand for 1 minute so the whey does not turn grainy.
Whisk in the whey and cinnamon quickly until smooth, adding a splash of water if it is too thick.
Pour into a bowl and top with the blueberries.
tip: Always add whey off the heat; boiling it makes it clump.

name: Apple cinnamon GF porridge
steps: Dice the apple into small cubes, leaving the skin on for extra fibre.
Put the oats, soy drink, apple and cinnamon in a saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cook for 6–7 minutes, stirring regularly, until the oats are creamy and the apple has softened.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with the maple syrup.
tip: Stir in 20 g pea protein after cooking to push it above 25 g of protein.

name: Scrambled eggs on toast
steps: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and whisk with a fork until the yolks and whites are fully combined.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over low-medium heat until it just foams.
Pour in the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula, pushing the set egg from the edges to the centre, for about 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look slightly wet; they will finish cooking in their own heat.
Toast the bread meanwhile, then pile the eggs on top with snipped chives, black pepper and the tomatoes on the side.
tip: For extra protein without much extra fat, add 100 ml egg whites to the whisked eggs.

name: Veggie omelette
steps: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a 20 cm nonstick pan over medium heat and fry the diced pepper for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the spinach and stir for 30 seconds until it wilts.
Pour in the eggs, tilt the pan to spread them, and cook for 2 minutes, lifting the edges so the raw egg runs underneath.
When the top is almost set, crumble over the feta, fold the omelette in half and slide it onto a plate.
tip: Swap the feta for 30 g smoked tofu to make it lactose-free.

name: Shakshuka
ingredients: 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, chilli flakes
steps: Heat the oil in a wide frying pan with a lid over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper for 6–8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and a pinch of chilli and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the tomatoes, season with salt and simmer for 8–10 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Make 5 small wells with a spoon and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook on low heat for 5–7 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Scatter with herbs and serve straight from the pan.
tip: The tomato sauce can be made 2 days ahead; reheat it until bubbling before adding the eggs.

name: Egg muffin cups
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (fan 160 °C) and lightly oil a 9-hole muffin tin or use silicone cups.
Chop the spinach and divide it with the pepper and spring onions between the holes.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper and pour the mixture over the vegetables until each cup is about three-quarters full.
Sprinkle the cheese on top.
Bake for 18–20 minutes until puffed and set in the centre; a knife inserted should come out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin, then run a knife around each one to release; 3 cups make one serving.
tip: They keep 4 days in the fridge and reheat in 30 seconds in the microwave.

name: Avocado egg toast
steps: Bring a small pan of water to a bare simmer and add a dash of vinegar.
Stir the water to make a gentle whirlpool, crack in the eggs one at a time and poach for 3 minutes for runny yolks.
Toast the sourdough meanwhile.
Mash the avocado with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt and spread it thickly on the toast.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon, drain on kitchen paper and set them on the toast with a pinch of chilli flakes.
tip: Use gluten-free bread to make it gluten-free; mash the avocado with lemon right away so leftovers do not brown.

name: Protein pancakes
steps: Blend the oats to a fine flour in a blender, then add the whey, egg, banana, milk and baking powder and blend until smooth.
Rest the batter for 2 minutes while you heat a nonstick pan over medium-low heat with a few drops of oil.
Pour in about 3 tablespoons of batter per pancake and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear on the surface.
Flip and cook for another minute until golden and springy.
Stack the pancakes and top with the berries.
tip: Too low a heat makes them dry, too high burns the whey; medium-low is the sweet spot.

name: Banana oat pancakes (GF)
ingredients: ½ tsp baking powder, pinch of cinnamon
steps: Blend the oats, eggs, banana, baking powder and cinnamon until you have a thick, smooth batter.
Heat a lightly oiled nonstick pan over medium-low heat.
Spoon in small rounds of batter, about 8 cm wide, and cook for 2 minutes until the edges look set.
Flip carefully and cook for 1 more minute.
Serve warm topped with the raspberries.
tip: Riper bananas mean sweeter pancakes, so no syrup is needed.

name: Skyr berry bowl
steps: Thaw frozen berries for 1 minute in the microwave if using frozen, so they release some juice.
Spoon the skyr into a bowl and stir it until smooth and glossy.
Top with the berries and their juice.
Scatter over the puffed rice for crunch just before eating and drizzle with honey.
tip: At bedtime, skip the puffed rice and honey for a lighter, slow-digesting protein bowl.

name: Greek yogurt granola bowl
steps: Spoon the Greek yogurt into a bowl.
Dice the apple into small cubes and scatter it over the yogurt.
Sprinkle the granola on top just before eating so it stays crunchy.
Finish with a thin drizzle of honey.
tip: Pack the granola separately in a small box if you are taking this to work.

name: Cottage cheese toast
steps: Toast the rye bread until crisp at the edges.
Drain any liquid from the cottage cheese and spread it thickly over the toast.
Lay the cucumber slices on top, overlapping them slightly.
Finish with torn dill and plenty of black pepper.
tip: Add 2 slices of smoked salmon for an extra 13 g of protein.

name: Smoked salmon bagel
ingredients: 1 tsp capers, a few thin slices of red onion, lemon
steps: Slice the bagel in half and toast it lightly.
Spread both halves with the cream cheese.
Layer the smoked salmon over the bottom half.
Scatter over the capers and red onion, add a squeeze of lemon and close the bagel.
tip: Wrap tightly in baking paper to eat on the go; it holds well for 3 hours in a cool bag.

name: Tofu scramble
ingredients: ½ tsp turmeric, pinch of black salt (kala namak) or salt
steps: Pat the tofu dry with kitchen paper and crumble it with your fingers into rough, egg-sized pieces.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 4 minutes until lightly golden.
Sprinkle in the turmeric, nutritional yeast and black salt and stir until the tofu turns evenly yellow.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, then fold in the spinach until just wilted.
Taste, season with pepper and serve hot.
tip: Black salt gives a convincingly eggy flavour; find it in Indian grocers.

name: Breakfast burrito
steps: Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper and scramble them in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat for 3 minutes until just set.
Warm the black beans in a small pan or the microwave for 1 minute, lightly crushing some with a fork.
Heat the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds per side so it becomes pliable.
Lay the beans, eggs, cheese and salsa down the middle, fold in the sides and roll it up tightly.
Toast seam-side down in the pan for 1 minute to seal it.
tip: Wrap cooled burritos in foil and freeze; reheat from frozen at 200 °C for 20 minutes.

name: Turkey & egg wrap
steps: Whisk the eggs and cook them in a nonstick pan over medium heat as a thin flat omelette, about 2 minutes.
Warm the tortilla for 20 seconds in a dry pan.
Lay the omelette on the tortilla, then the turkey, rocket and salsa.
Roll it up tightly, tucking in the ends, and cut it in half on the diagonal.
tip: Use a corn tortilla to make it gluten-free.

name: Chicken sausage hash
steps: Dice the potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes and microwave them in a covered bowl for 5 minutes until just tender.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and brown the sliced sausages for 5 minutes, then set them aside.
Add the potatoes to the same pan in a single layer and fry for 6–8 minutes, turning only occasionally, until crisp.
Add the onion, pepper and paprika and cook for 5 more minutes until soft.
Return the sausages, toss everything together and season before serving.
tip: Check the sausage label: many are gluten-free, but some contain rusk or breadcrumbs.

name: Green smoothie bowl
steps: Peel and slice the banana before freezing; frozen pieces make the bowl thick and cold.
Blend the frozen banana, spinach, soy drink and pea protein on high for 45 seconds, scraping down once, until thick and smooth.
Pour into a bowl; it should be thick enough to hold toppings.
Slice the kiwi and arrange it on top with the almonds.
tip: Add the soy drink gradually; too much makes a smoothie, not a bowl.

name: Berry protein smoothie
steps: Pour the milk into the blender first so the blades turn freely.
Add the whey, frozen berries and banana.
Blend on high for 30–45 seconds until completely smooth.
Drink straight away or pour into a shaker bottle to take to the gym.
tip: Use lactose-free milk and a lactose-free whey isolate if dairy bothers you.

name: Coffee protein shake
ingredients: 150 ml cold brew or cooled coffee
steps: Brew the coffee ahead and let it cool, or use cold brew.
Add the coffee, milk, whey, oats and honey to a blender.
Blend for 45 seconds until the oats are fully broken down.
Pour over ice and drink right away.
tip: A chocolate whey works brilliantly here for a mocha flavour.

name: Quinoa breakfast bowl
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve under cold water for 30 seconds to remove its bitter coating.
Simmer it with the soy drink and cinnamon in a covered pan over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is absorbed.
Let it stand off the heat for 2 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Top with the sliced peach and walnuts and drizzle with maple syrup.
tip: Cook a double batch; cold quinoa porridge keeps 3 days and reheats with a splash of milk.

name: Mango chia pudding
steps: Whisk the pea protein into the coconut drink until smooth.
Stir in the chia seeds, wait 10 minutes and stir again to break up any clumps.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight until thick and spoonable.
Top with the diced mango before serving.
tip: Frozen mango cubes thaw overnight on top of the pudding and save chopping time.

name: Savoury oats with egg
steps: Simmer the oats with 250 ml water and a pinch of salt over medium heat for 5 minutes until creamy.
Stir the spinach through for the last minute until wilted.
Meanwhile fry the eggs in a nonstick pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the edges crisp.
Spoon the oats into a bowl, season with soy sauce and sesame oil and top with the eggs and spring onion.
tip: Swap soy sauce for tamari and the oats for gluten-free oats to make it gluten-free.

name: Huevos rancheros
steps: Warm the salsa and black beans together in a small pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Toast the corn tortillas in a dry pan for 1 minute per side until spotted and pliable.
Fry the eggs in a nonstick pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until the whites are set.
Lay the tortillas on a plate, spoon over the beans and salsa and top each with an egg.
Crumble over the cheese and add sliced avocado.
tip: Skip the feta to make it lactose-free; corn tortillas keep it gluten-free.

name: Protein French toast
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Soak each slice of bread for 20 seconds per side so it absorbs the mixture without falling apart.
Cook in a lightly oiled nonstick pan over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden and set in the middle.
Serve with the Greek yogurt, sliced strawberries and a drizzle of maple syrup.
tip: Day-old bread soaks up the egg better and gives a crisper result.

name: Turkish eggs (çılbır)
ingredients: 1 small garlic clove, grated; 1 tsp Aleppo pepper or paprika; dill
steps: Stir the grated garlic and a pinch of salt into the yogurt and spread it in a shallow bowl so it comes to room temperature.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks runny.
Melt the butter in a small pan over low heat, add the Aleppo pepper and swirl for 30 seconds until it turns red.
Lift the eggs onto the yogurt, spoon over the spiced butter and scatter with dill.
Serve with the warmed pita for dipping.
tip: Use gluten-free bread or skip the pita to make it gluten-free.

name: Buckwheat porridge
steps: Rinse the buckwheat groats in a sieve.
Simmer them with the soy drink and a pinch of salt in a covered pan over low heat for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and creamy.
Stir in the diced pear and cinnamon for the last 2 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the pumpkin seeds.
tip: Buckwheat is naturally gluten-free despite the name.

name: Ricotta & honey toast
steps: Toast the sourdough until golden.
Spread the ricotta thickly over each slice.
Top with the sliced fig, or a sliced pear when figs are out of season.
Drizzle with honey and finish with a little black pepper.
tip: Stir 15 g whey into the ricotta to add 12 g of protein.

name: Protein waffles
steps: Heat the waffle iron and brush it lightly with oil.
Blend the oats to a fine flour, then whisk in the whey and baking powder.
Add the eggs and milk and whisk to a thick, pourable batter; rest for 3 minutes.
Ladle the batter into the iron and cook for 4–5 minutes until golden and crisp.
Serve two waffles per person with the berries.
tip: Freeze cooled waffles between sheets of baking paper and toast straight from frozen.

name: Egg white omelette
steps: Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and cook the mushrooms for 3 minutes until golden.
Whisk the egg whites with the whole egg and a pinch of salt.
Add the spinach to the pan, let it wilt, then pour in the eggs.
Cook for 2–3 minutes, lifting the edges so the liquid runs under, until set.
Scatter over the tomato, fold in half and serve.
tip: The single whole egg adds flavour and colour without much fat.

name: Homemade nut granola
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (fan 140 °C) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Roughly chop the nuts and mix them with the oats, seeds, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl.
Warm the maple syrup and oil together, pour over the dry mix and stir until everything is evenly coated.
Spread in a thin layer on the tray and bake for 20–25 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden.
Let it cool completely on the tray; it crisps up as it cools.
Store in an airtight jar and serve 60 g with milk or yogurt.
tip: Keeps for 3 weeks in an airtight jar; add dried fruit only after baking so it does not burn.

name: PB banana toast
steps: Toast the bread until golden.
Spread the peanut butter thinly while the toast is hot so it melts slightly.
Slice the banana and lay it on top.
Dust with cinnamon and eat straight away.
tip: Add a glass of soy drink on the side for an extra 8 g of protein.

name: Ham & egg muffin
steps: Split and toast the English muffin.
Whisk the eggs and pour them into a lightly oiled small pan over medium heat; cook as a thick folded omelette for 3 minutes.
Warm the ham in the same pan for 30 seconds.
Layer the ham, egg and cheese on the muffin, close it and let the heat melt the cheese.
tip: Wrap in foil to keep it warm on the way to work.

name: Chicken ginger congee
steps: Rinse the rice, then put it in a large pot with the stock and ginger.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a low simmer and cook for 30 minutes, stirring often so it does not catch, until the rice breaks down into a silky porridge.
Slice the chicken thinly and stir it in for the last 8 minutes until cooked through and white in the centre.
Add more water if it gets too thick; it should flow slowly off a spoon.
Season with tamari and serve topped with spring onions.
tip: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; it thickens when cold, so loosen it with hot water when reheating.

name: Rösti with fried eggs
steps: Grate the potatoes coarsely, then squeeze them hard in a clean tea towel to remove as much liquid as possible.
Mix with the onion and ½ tsp salt.
Heat the oil in a 20 cm nonstick pan over medium heat, press the potato into an even cake and cook for 8–10 minutes until deep golden underneath.
Slide it onto a plate, flip it back into the pan and cook the other side for 8 minutes.
Fry the eggs in the same pan beside the rösti or in a second pan, and serve the eggs on top with the tomatoes.
tip: Use potatoes boiled the day before for the classic Bernese rösti; they hold together better.

name: Rice cakes, banana & honey
steps: Lay the rice cakes on a plate or in a lunch box.
Slice the banana into thin rounds and arrange them over the rice cakes.
Drizzle with the honey and dust with cinnamon.
Eat 60–90 minutes before training so the fast carbs are ready when you start.
tip: Carry the banana whole and assemble at the gym so the rice cakes stay crisp.

name: White toast & jam
steps: Toast the bread until golden.
Spread the jam evenly over both slices without butter to keep the fat low.
Eat with the half banana about an hour before your session.
Drink a glass of water alongside to start well hydrated.
tip: White bread is the right choice here: low fibre means quick digestion and no stomach upset mid-session.

name: Light rice pudding
ingredients: 1 tsp vanilla extract, pinch of cinnamon
steps: Rinse the rice, then put it in a heavy saucepan with the milk and vanilla.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring so it does not stick.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 25–30 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the rice is soft and creamy.
Stir in the honey off the heat, then let it cool slightly; it thickens as it stands.
Serve warm or cold, dusted with cinnamon; one quarter of the pot is a serving.
tip: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in portion pots; loosen with a splash of milk before eating.

name: Bagel with honey
steps: Split the bagel and toast it lightly.
Drizzle the honey over both halves while warm so it soaks in.
Eat with the strawberries on the side.
Allow 60–90 minutes before training for a big session.
tip: For a morning session with no time to eat, half a bagel 30 minutes before is enough.

name: Banana oat shake
steps: Put the oats in the blender first and blitz them for 10 seconds into a fine powder.
Add the milk, banana and honey.
Blend for 30 seconds until smooth.
Drink 45–60 minutes before training.
tip: Blending the oats to powder first keeps the shake smooth and easy on the stomach.

name: Low-fat fruit yogurt cup
steps: Spoon the fruit yogurt into a cup or small jar.
Slice the peach and add it on top.
Sprinkle the cornflakes over just before eating so they stay crunchy.
Eat about an hour before training.
tip: Tinned peaches in juice, drained, work just as well.

name: Pretzels & grapes
steps: Wash the grapes and pull them off the stalk.
Pack them in a box with the pretzels.
Eat 60 minutes before training; the salt on the pretzels helps with fluid retention on hot days.
Follow with a glass of water.
tip: Great before long endurance sessions, when you need carbs and a little sodium.

name: Cream of rice with whey
steps: Bring 250 ml water to the boil in a small pan.
Whisk in the cream of rice and simmer for 2–3 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick.
Take off the heat, wait 1 minute, then whisk in the whey until smooth.
Top with blueberries and honey.
tip: Very gentle on the stomach, which makes it ideal 60 minutes before heavy squats or intervals.

name: Umeboshi onigiri
ingredients: ½ sheet nori, cut into strips
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then cook it with 110 ml water in a covered pan: 2 minutes on high, then 12 minutes on the lowest heat.
Rest the rice covered for 10 minutes, then spread it on a plate to cool until just warm.
Wet your hands, rub them with a pinch of salt and take half the rice.
Press a hollow in the middle, add half the plum and close the rice around it, squeezing into a firm triangle.
Repeat with the rest, sprinkle with sesame and wrap each with a strip of nori.
tip: Wrap in cling film; onigiri keep fresh for a day at cool room temperature.

name: Salmon onigiri
steps: Cook the rinsed rice with 120 ml water in a covered pan for 2 minutes on high and 12 minutes on the lowest heat, then rest it for 10 minutes.
Stir the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt into the warm rice.
Flake the salmon with a fork, removing any skin.
With wet, salted hands shape the rice into two triangles, each with a spoon of salmon pressed into the centre.
Wrap each with nori just before eating so it stays crisp.
tip: Tuna works the same way and costs less.

name: Mango lassi
steps: Peel and chop the mango, or use frozen chunks.
Blend the mango, yogurt, milk and cardamom for 30 seconds until smooth and frothy.
Pour over a few ice cubes.
Drink 45–60 minutes before training.
tip: Frozen mango makes it thick and cold without diluting it with ice.

name: Crumpets with honey
steps: Toast the crumpets until crisp on the outside, about 4 minutes.
Drizzle the honey over them so it runs into the holes.
Serve with the half banana sliced on top or alongside.
Eat about an hour before you train.
tip: Skip butter before a session: fat slows digestion.

name: Applesauce rice cakes
steps: Lay the rice cakes out on a plate or pack them flat in a lunch box.
Spread each with a generous spoon of applesauce.
Drizzle with maple syrup and dust with cinnamon.
Eat right away before the rice cakes soften.
tip: Single-serve applesauce pouches make this easy to assemble at the gym.

name: Sweet couscous with dates
steps: Put the couscous in a bowl with the cinnamon and pour over 90 ml boiling water.
Cover with a plate and leave for 5 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and stir in the chopped dates and a little orange zest.
Top with the orange segments and eat warm or cold.
tip: Make it in a jar the night before for an on-the-go pre-session meal.

name: Pineapple ginger smoothie
steps: Peel and roughly chop the ginger.
Put the pineapple, banana, ginger and coconut water in a blender.
Blend for 40 seconds until completely smooth.
Drink 30–60 minutes before training; the coconut water adds potassium for hot sessions.
tip: Use frozen pineapple chunks for a thick, ice-cold drink.

name: Ham baguette
steps: Split the baguette lengthways without cutting all the way through.
Spread the inside thinly with mustard instead of butter to keep it lean.
Fill with the ham and sliced gherkins.
Wrap in paper and eat 1–2 hours before training.
tip: No butter keeps the fat low so it digests quickly before a session.

name: Turkey rice cakes
steps: Spread each rice cake with a little mustard.
Top with folded turkey slices.
Add thin cucumber rounds and black pepper.
Eat straight away so the rice cakes stay crisp.
tip: A light savoury option 60–90 minutes before training.

name: Pre-gym chicken rice
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in salted boiling water for 12 minutes, then drain.
Cut the chicken into strips and cook it in a nonstick pan with a few drops of water over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes until no longer pink inside.
Steam or boil the carrot slices for 5 minutes until tender.
Toss everything with the tamari and herbs and eat 2 hours before a long or hard session.
tip: Keep it plain: no creamy sauces or oily dressings before training.

name: Strawberry skyr smoothie
steps: Hull the strawberries and halve any large ones so they blend evenly.
Blend everything for 30–40 seconds until smooth.
Pour into a bottle to take with you.
Drink an hour before training or straight after as a recovery drink.
tip: Frozen strawberries make it thicker and colder.

name: Dates & milk
steps: Pit the dates by slitting them along one side and pulling out the stone.
Pour a glass of cold skimmed milk.
Eat the dates with the milk 60 minutes before training.
For a quicker fuel-up, blend both into a shake.
tip: A traditional and very effective way to break a fast before an evening workout during Ramadan.

name: Fruit salad with honey
ingredients: a few mint leaves, squeeze of lime
steps: Cut the melon into bite-size cubes.
Slice the banana and halve the grapes.
Toss everything with a squeeze of lime, the honey and torn mint.
Eat within an hour of making, about 60 minutes before you train.
tip: The lime stops the banana from browning if you prepare it ahead.

name: Vanilla semolina pudding
steps: Heat the soy drink with the vanilla in a small pan over medium heat until steaming.
Whisk in the semolina in a thin stream to avoid lumps.
Simmer on low for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Sweeten with maple syrup and top with raspberries.
tip: Use dairy milk instead of soy for a classic Austrian Griessbrei.

name: Banana & sports drink
steps: Mix the sports drink if you use powder, following the label.
Eat the banana and rice cakes 30–45 minutes before starting.
Sip the sports drink during the warm-up and the first part of a long session.
Keep sipping during sessions longer than 75 minutes.
tip: For races or sessions over 90 minutes, add one energy gel every 30–45 minutes.

name: Honey toast & cottage cheese
steps: Toast the bread until golden and crisp, about 2–3 minutes.
Spread the cottage cheese over the toast.
Drizzle the honey over the top while the toast is still warm.
Eat 60–90 minutes before training for carbs plus a little protein.
tip: Low-fat cottage cheese keeps it light enough before a session.

name: Hummus & veggie sticks
steps: Peel the carrot and cut it into finger-length sticks.
Cut the cucumber and pepper into sticks of the same size.
Spoon the hummus into a small pot.
Pack the vegetables standing upright in a box next to the hummus for easy dipping.
tip: Add a few rice crackers if you need more carbs after a session.

name: Salted edamame
steps: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil.
Add the frozen edamame and cook for 4–5 minutes until bright green and tender.
Drain well and toss with flaky salt, a pinch of chilli and a squeeze of lime.
Eat warm or pack them cold for later.
tip: Buy edamame in pods for a slower, more satisfying snack; double the weight to account for the pods.

name: Crispy roasted chickpeas
ingredients: 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp ground cumin, salt
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C).
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then dry them very well with a tea towel, rubbing off loose skins.
Toss with the oil, spices and salt and spread on a lined baking tray in a single layer.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, shaking the tray every 10 minutes, until deep golden and crunchy.
Let them cool on the tray; they crisp further as they cool.
tip: Store in a jar with the lid loose; sealed tightly they soften within a day.

name: Protein energy balls
steps: Blitz the oats in a food processor for 15 seconds to break them up a little.
Add the whey, cocoa, peanut butter and honey and pulse until the mixture clumps together.
If it is too dry, add water a teaspoon at a time; if too sticky, add a spoon of oats.
Roll into 12 walnut-sized balls with damp hands.
Chill for 30 minutes to firm up; two balls are one serving.
tip: They keep 1 week in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

name: Apple & peanut butter
steps: Core the apple and cut it into 8 wedges.
Spoon the peanut butter into a small pot for dipping.
Squeeze a little lemon over the wedges if you pack them for later, so they do not brown.
Dip the apple wedges into the peanut butter as you eat.
tip: Almond butter is a peanut-free alternative with almost the same macros.

name: Tuna on rice crackers
steps: Drain the tuna well and flake it into a bowl.
Mix in the diced cucumber, a good squeeze of lemon, pepper and chives.
Spoon onto the rice crackers just before eating.
Keep the topping and crackers separate if you are packing it.
tip: A spoon of Greek yogurt makes the tuna creamier without mayonnaise.

name: Trail mix
steps: Weigh out the nuts and raisins.
Mix them in a small bag or tin.
Make several bags at once for the week.
Eat as an afternoon snack on long days when you need energy-dense food.
tip: Nuts are calorie-dense, so weigh the portion rather than eating from the bag.

name: Cottage cheese & pineapple
steps: Drain any liquid from the cottage cheese.
Spoon it into a bowl and stir until smooth.
Dice the pineapple into small cubes and scatter it on top.
Eat as an afternoon snack or 30–60 minutes before bed.
tip: Tinned pineapple in juice, drained, works well and lasts longer.

name: Boiled eggs & tomatoes
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 8 minutes for firm but creamy yolks.
Transfer them to cold water for 2 minutes, then peel.
Halve the eggs and season with salt and pepper.
Serve with the cherry tomatoes.
tip: Boil 6 at once; unpeeled eggs keep 5 days in the fridge.

name: Beef jerky & apple
steps: Open the jerky pack and weigh out the portion.
Wash the apple and cut it into wedges if you prefer.
Eat together as a portable protein and carb snack.
Drink water alongside, as jerky is salty.
tip: Choose a jerky with less than 10 g sugar per 100 g; many brands are heavily sweetened.

name: Baked tofu bites
ingredients: 1 tsp cornflour, ½ tsp garlic powder
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C) and line a tray with baking paper.
Press the tofu between kitchen paper under a heavy pan for 10 minutes, then cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Toss with the tamari and sesame oil, then dust with the cornflour and garlic powder.
Spread out on the tray and bake for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and chewy.
Eat warm or cold; a third of the batch is a serving.
tip: They keep 4 days in the fridge and are great added to salads.

name: Chocolate skyr mousse
steps: Sift the cocoa into a bowl so there are no lumps.
Add the skyr and honey and whisk for 1 minute until smooth and airy.
Top with the raspberries, lightly crushing a few so their juice runs in.
Eat straight away or chill for 20 minutes for a firmer set.
tip: A few drops of vanilla or a pinch of salt makes the chocolate taste richer.

name: Soy yogurt with berries
steps: Spoon the soy yogurt into a bowl or jar.
Add the berries; frozen ones will thaw in 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with pumpkin seeds.
Pack with a lid if you take it to work.
tip: Stir in 15 g pea protein to double the protein.

name: Salmon cucumber bites
steps: Slice the cucumber into 1 cm thick rounds.
Spread each round with a little cream cheese.
Top with a folded piece of smoked salmon.
Finish with dill, black pepper and a few drops of lemon.
tip: Great for guests too; make them no more than 2 hours ahead.

name: Spiced popcorn
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan with a lid over medium-high heat and add 3 kernels.
When they pop, add the rest of the kernels, cover and shake the pan.
Cook for 2–3 minutes, shaking often, until the popping slows to 2 seconds between pops.
Tip into a bowl and toss with paprika and salt.
tip: Air-popped popcorn is a high-fibre, high-volume snack for evenings.

name: Bresaola rocket rolls
steps: Lay out the bresaola slices on a board.
Place a few rocket leaves and a shaving of parmesan on each.
Squeeze over a little lemon and roll them up.
Season with black pepper and eat.
tip: Swiss Bündnerfleisch is the same idea and works perfectly.

name: Protein bar & fruit
steps: Keep a bar in your gym bag for days with no time to cook.
Eat it with the orange straight after training.
Drink at least 500 ml of water with it.
Have a full meal within 2–3 hours.
tip: Check labels: choose bars with at least 20 g protein and under 10 g sugar.

name: Hummus rice cake stack
steps: Spread the hummus over the rice cakes.
Top with tomato and cucumber slices.
Season with pepper and a pinch of za'atar or paprika.
Eat right away, before the rice cakes soften.
tip: Swap rice cakes for rye crispbread for extra fibre.

name: Chocolate milk
steps: Chill the chocolate milk.
Drink it with the banana within 30 minutes after training.
Follow with a full meal within 2 hours.
Choose a version with at least 3 g protein per 100 ml.
tip: Research shows chocolate milk is as good as many commercial recovery drinks.

name: Casein protein pudding
steps: Put the casein in a bowl.
Add the milk a little at a time, stirring hard; casein thickens into a pudding.
Stop when it reaches a thick, mousse-like texture.
Top with blueberries and eat 30–60 minutes before bed.
tip: Casein digests slowly, feeding your muscles through the night.

name: Cottage cheese & walnuts
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl.
Roughly chop the walnuts.
Scatter the nuts on top and dust with cinnamon.
Eat as a late snack, 30–60 minutes before bed.
tip: Swap the walnuts for 10 g pumpkin seeds if you avoid tree nuts.

name: Quark with cinnamon
steps: Stir the quark until smooth and creamy; add a splash of milk if it is very thick.
Mix in the cinnamon and honey.
Top with the raspberries, lightly crushing a few so their juice runs in.
Eat 30–60 minutes before bed.
tip: Quark is one of the cheapest sources of slow-digesting protein.

name: Skyr chia bowl
steps: Stir the chia seeds into the skyr.
Leave for 5 minutes so they swell slightly.
Top with the blueberries just before eating.
Eat 30–60 minutes before bed.
tip: Make it in the morning and let it set in the fridge all day.

name: Vegan bedtime protein bowl
steps: Whisk the soy protein into the soy yogurt until smooth.
Stir in the ground flaxseed and cinnamon.
Rest for 2 minutes so it thickens.
Eat 30–60 minutes before bed.
tip: Soy protein contains all essential amino acids, much like dairy protein.

name: Savoury cottage cheese
steps: Dice the cucumber into small cubes and pat them dry with kitchen paper.
Mix it into the cottage cheese with the snipped chives.
Season with black pepper.
Eat as a savoury late-evening snack.
tip: A rye crispbread on the side adds crunch and fibre.

name: Casein hot cocoa
steps: Heat the milk in a small pan over medium heat until steaming but not boiling.
Whisk the casein and cocoa in a mug with a splash of cold milk to a smooth paste.
Pour in the hot milk, whisking constantly.
Sweeten with a little sweetener if you like and sip before bed.
tip: Keep the milk below boiling so the protein stays smooth.

name: Greek yogurt, honey & almond
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Roughly chop the almonds.
Scatter them over the yogurt and drizzle with honey.
Eat as an afternoon snack or before bed.
tip: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes for extra flavour.

name: Silken tofu cocoa pudding
steps: Drain the silken tofu and pat it dry with kitchen paper.
Blend it with the cocoa, maple syrup, soy protein and vanilla for 1 minute until completely smooth.
Divide between two glasses.
Chill for 30 minutes to set; one glass is a serving.
tip: Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.

name: Kefir berry drink
steps: Blend the kefir, berries and whey for 20 seconds.
Pour into a glass and stir once if the berries have settled.
Sip slowly as an evening drink.
Store any leftover in a sealed bottle for up to a day.
tip: Kefir is often tolerated better than milk thanks to its lower lactose content.

name: Turkey cucumber rolls
steps: Cut the cucumber into thin batons.
Spread each turkey slice with a little cream cheese.
Roll a cucumber baton inside each slice.
Eat as a light, savoury evening snack.
tip: Use hummus instead of cream cheese for a lactose-free version.

name: Warm oat & casein mug
steps: Heat the milk with the oats in a small pan over low heat for 3 minutes, stirring.
Take it off the heat and cool for 30 seconds.
Whisk in the casein until smooth.
Pour into a mug, dust with nutmeg and sip before bed.
tip: Casein contains lactose, so if you are very sensitive use a soy protein instead.

name: Teriyaki chicken bowl
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in 160 ml water in a covered pan: bring to the boil, then simmer on the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest for 5.
Cut the chicken into bite-size strips and season with pepper.
Sear the chicken in a hot nonstick pan over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes, turning, until golden and no longer pink inside.
Pour in the teriyaki sauce and toss for 1 minute until the chicken is glossy and sticky.
Steam the broccoli for 4 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Spoon the rice into a bowl, add the chicken and broccoli and finish with sesame seeds and spring onion.
tip: Use tamari-based teriyaki to make it gluten-free; the chicken keeps 3 days for lunch boxes.

name: Chicken fajita wraps
steps: Slice the chicken into thin strips and toss with the fajita spice, half the oil and a squeeze of lime.
Heat a large frying pan over high heat until very hot, add the chicken and cook for 5–6 minutes until charred at the edges and cooked through; set aside.
Add the remaining oil, the peppers and the onion and stir-fry for 5 minutes until softened but still with some bite.
Return the chicken to the pan and toss everything together for 1 minute.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 15 seconds per side.
Fill each tortilla with the chicken and vegetables, add salsa, roll up and serve two per person.
tip: Use corn tortillas to make it gluten-free; leftover filling makes a great rice bowl next day.

name: Chicken & sweet potato tray
ingredients: 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, salt
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (fan 200 °C).
Cut the sweet potatoes into 2 cm chunks and toss on a large tray with the onion, half the oil, paprika and salt.
Roast for 15 minutes until the edges start to colour.
Cut the chicken into large chunks, toss with the remaining oil and garlic powder, and add it to the tray with the broccoli florets.
Roast for another 18–20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (74 °C in the centre) and the sweet potato is caramelised.
Divide between two plates or boxes.
tip: Doubles easily on two trays for four days of meal-prep lunches.

name: Chicken pesto pasta
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta for 1 minute less than the packet says.
Meanwhile cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and fry it in a lightly oiled pan over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add the tomatoes to the chicken and cook for 2 minutes until they start to soften.
Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain the pasta and add it to the pan with the pesto and spinach.
Toss over low heat with a splash of pasta water until the spinach wilts and the sauce coats the pasta.
Serve topped with grated parmesan.
tip: Store lunch boxes with a little extra pasta water so the pasta does not dry out.

name: Light chicken Caesar
steps: Season the chicken, then cook it in a hot griddle or nonstick pan over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through; rest for 3 minutes and slice.
Toast the bread cubes in the same pan for 3 minutes until crisp to make croutons.
Tear the romaine into large pieces and toss with the dressing and a squeeze of lemon.
Top with the sliced chicken, croutons and shaved parmesan.
tip: Keep the dressing separate in a small pot if you pack it for lunch.

name: Chicken & chickpea curry
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry powder, 2 garlic cloves, 1 thumb ginger
steps: Fry the onion in a splash of oil in a large pan over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and stir for 1 minute.
Add the chicken, cut into chunks, and stir for 3 minutes until sealed on all sides.
Pour in the tomatoes and coconut milk, add the chickpeas, and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Meanwhile cook the rice in plenty of salted water for 10–12 minutes and drain.
Stir the spinach into the curry for the last 2 minutes until wilted, then season with salt.
Serve a quarter of the curry over a quarter of the rice.
tip: Freezes well for up to 3 months; freeze the curry without the rice.

name: Chicken souvlaki pita
steps: Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes and marinate with the oil, oregano, lemon zest and juice for at least 10 minutes.
Thread onto skewers, or leave loose, and cook on a hot griddle or under a grill for 10–12 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Warm the pitas in the pan for 30 seconds per side.
Open each pita, spread with tzatziki and fill with the chicken, tomato and red onion.
tip: Soak wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes so they do not burn.

name: Chicken veg stir-fry noodles
steps: Cook the noodles according to the packet, usually 4 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Slice the chicken thinly and stir-fry it in half the sesame oil in a very hot wok for 4–5 minutes until cooked through; set aside.
Add the remaining oil, the garlic, ginger and vegetables and stir-fry for 3 minutes over high heat.
Return the chicken, add the noodles and soy sauce and toss for 2 minutes until everything is hot and glossy.
Serve straight away while the noodles are hot and glossy.
tip: Rice noodles and tamari make this gluten- and egg-free.

name: Chicken quinoa salad
steps: Rinse the quinoa, then simmer it in 120 ml salted water in a covered pan for 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed; fluff and cool.
Cook the chicken in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat for 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through, then rest and slice.
Dice the cucumber and halve the tomatoes.
Whisk the oil with lemon juice and salt, then toss with the quinoa, vegetables and parsley.
Top with the chicken and pomegranate seeds.
tip: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; add the dressing on the day for the crunchiest result.

name: Tandoori chicken & rice
steps: Mix the yogurt, tandoori spice, lemon juice and salt, then coat the chicken pieces and marinate for at least 15 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 220 °C (fan 200 °C) and line a tray with foil.
Spread the chicken out on the tray and roast for 20–22 minutes until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Meanwhile cook the rice in salted boiling water for 10–12 minutes and drain.
Dice the cucumber and serve it with the rice and chicken, with lemon wedges on the side.
tip: Coconut yogurt makes a lactose-free marinade that works just as well.

name: Chicken burrito bowl
steps: Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, drain and stir in lime juice.
Rub the chicken with taco seasoning and cook in a hot pan over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through, then slice.
Warm the black beans and sweetcorn together in a small pan for 3 minutes.
Build the bowl: lettuce, rice, beans and corn, chicken, salsa and sliced avocado.
tip: Make four bowls at once without the avocado and add it fresh each day.

name: Chicken vegetable soup
steps: Put the whole chicken breasts in a large pot with the stock and bay leaf, bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 15 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and set aside to cool slightly.
Add the carrots, celery, leek and diced potatoes to the stock and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Shred the chicken with two forks and return it to the pot.
Simmer for 2 more minutes, season with salt and pepper and stir in the parsley.
tip: Freezes well for 3 months; add a handful of pasta when reheating for more carbs.

name: Chicken satay bowl
ingredients: 1 lime, ½ tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp honey
steps: Cook the rice in 320 ml water in a covered pan for 12 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, chilli, honey and 4 tbsp hot water into a pourable sauce.
Cut the chicken into strips, coat with a third of the sauce and cook in a hot pan for 6–7 minutes until charred and cooked through.
Blanch the green beans in boiling water for 4 minutes and drain.
Serve the chicken over rice with the beans and sliced cucumber, drizzled with the remaining sauce.
tip: Tamari instead of soy sauce makes it gluten-free.

name: Lemon chicken & potatoes
ingredients: 4 garlic cloves (unpeeled), a few sprigs of thyme
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (fan 190 °C).
Toss the halved potatoes with half the oil, garlic, thyme and salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Rub the chicken with the remaining oil, lemon zest, salt and pepper and nestle it among the potatoes with lemon halves.
Roast for 18–20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are golden.
Boil the green beans for 4 minutes in the meantime.
Squeeze the roasted lemon over everything and serve.
tip: Squeeze the soft roasted garlic out of its skin and mash it into the potatoes.

name: Turkey bean chili
ingredients: 2 tsp chilli powder, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika
steps: Brown the turkey mince in a large pot with a splash of oil over high heat for 6 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon.
Add the chopped onion and pepper and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spices for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and beans.
Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Season the chili and serve over the rice.
tip: Freeze in portions; it tastes even better after a day in the fridge.

name: Turkey meatballs in tomato
steps: Mix the turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, oregano and salt and roll into 18 meatballs with damp hands.
Brown them in a lightly oiled pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, turning, until coloured all over.
Add the garlic and passata, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water for the time on the packet and drain.
Toss the pasta with some of the sauce and serve with six meatballs per person, topped with basil.
tip: Freeze the meatballs in their sauce; use gluten-free breadcrumbs and pasta if needed.

name: Turkey burger & wedges
ingredients: 1 tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp garlic powder
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (fan 200 °C).
Cut the sweet potato into wedges, toss with the oil and paprika and roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until crisp at the edges.
Mix the turkey with garlic powder, salt and pepper and shape two 2 cm thick patties.
Cook the patties in a hot pan over medium heat for 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through (no pink in the middle).
Toast the buns and build the burgers with lettuce and tomato; serve with the wedges.
tip: Turkey dries out easily, so take the patties off the heat as soon as they are cooked through.

name: Chicken shawarma plate
steps: Toss the chicken with the shawarma spice, a squeeze of lemon and salt.
Cover the bulgur with 240 ml boiling salted water, cover and leave for 15 minutes, then fluff.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes per side until charred and cooked through, then slice.
Whisk the tahini with the remaining lemon juice and 3 tbsp water to a pourable sauce.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes with parsley for a quick salad.
Serve the chicken over the bulgur with the salad and drizzle with tahini sauce.
tip: Use rice instead of bulgur to make it gluten-free.

name: Thai green chicken curry
steps: Cook the rice in 420 ml water in a covered pan for 12 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes.
Fry the curry paste in a large pan with 3 tbsp of the coconut milk over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the sliced chicken and stir for 3 minutes until sealed.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, bring to a simmer and add the beans and courgette.
Simmer for 8–10 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are tender, then season with fish sauce and lime.
Serve over the rice with Thai basil.
tip: Most green curry pastes contain shrimp paste; check the label if you avoid shellfish.

name: Chicken avocado wrap
steps: Slice the cooked chicken.
Mash the avocado with a pinch of salt and lime and spread it over the tortilla.
Add lettuce, sliced tomato, chicken and salsa down the middle.
Fold in the sides, roll tightly and cut in half.
tip: Wrap in foil or baking paper; it keeps well for lunch the same day.

name: Moroccan chicken couscous
steps: Pour 225 ml boiling salted water over the couscous, cover and leave for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Rub the chicken with ras el hanout and cook in a hot oiled pan over medium heat for 6 minutes per side until cooked through; rest and slice.
Dice the pepper and chop the apricots.
Stir the pepper, apricots, lemon juice and mint into the couscous.
Serve topped with the chicken; it is good warm or cold.
tip: Packs well for lunch and keeps 3 days in the fridge.

name: Baked chicken katsu curry
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (fan 190 °C) and put a rack over a baking tray.
Butterfly the chicken breasts, dip them in beaten egg and press into the panko on both sides.
Spray with oil and bake on the rack for 20–25 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile fry the onion and carrot in a pan for 5 minutes, add 400 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in the curry roux until thick.
Cook the rice in 220 ml water in a covered pan for 12 minutes and rest for 5.
Slice the katsu and serve over rice with the sauce poured alongside.
tip: Baking on a rack keeps the coating crisp underneath without deep-frying.

name: Chicken pho
ingredients: 1 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 slices ginger, 1 lime, chilli
steps: Toast the star anise and cinnamon in a dry pot over medium heat for 1 minute, then add the stock and ginger.
Bring to a simmer, add the whole chicken breasts and poach gently for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and shred it; season the broth with fish sauce and remove the spices.
Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the packet and divide between two deep bowls.
Top with the chicken and beansprouts and ladle over the boiling broth.
Finish with herbs, lime and chilli.
tip: Freeze the broth in portions for a 10-minute pho on busy nights.

name: Chicken egg fried rice
ingredients: 160 g rice (dry), cooked the day before
steps: Use cold cooked rice from the fridge; fresh rice turns mushy.
Heat half the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the diced chicken for 5 minutes until cooked through; set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the frozen vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Push everything to the side, scramble the eggs in the empty space for 1 minute, then add the rice.
Toss over high heat for 3 minutes, breaking up any clumps, then return the chicken and add the soy sauce.
Serve topped with spring onions.
tip: Use tamari to make it gluten-free.

name: Chicken cacciatore
steps: Season the chicken thighs and brown them in the oil in a large casserole over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side; set aside.
Add the onion, peppers, mushrooms and garlic and cook for 6 minutes until softened.
Pour in the tomatoes, add the rosemary and olives and return the chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes until the chicken is very tender.
Season and serve on its own for a low-carb dinner, or with potatoes or polenta.
tip: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

name: Jerk chicken, rice & peas
ingredients: 2 tbsp jerk seasoning, 1 lime, spring onion
steps: Rub the chicken with the jerk seasoning and marinate for at least 10 minutes.
Put the rice, beans, coconut milk, 200 ml water and a pinch of salt in a pan, bring to the boil, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Cook the chicken on a hot griddle or under the grill for 6–7 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Dice the mango with lime juice and spring onion for a quick salsa.
Serve the sliced chicken with the rice and peas and the mango salsa.
tip: Jerk seasoning is hot; use half the amount for a milder version.

name: One-pot lemon chicken orzo
steps: Cut the chicken into chunks and brown it in a lightly oiled deep pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes.
Add the orzo and stir for 1 minute, then pour in the stock and lemon zest.
Simmer for 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is tender and most of the stock is absorbed.
Stir in the spinach and lemon juice until wilted.
Serve topped with crumbled feta.
tip: The orzo keeps absorbing liquid, so add a splash of water when reheating.

name: Miso chicken ramen
steps: Boil the eggs for 6½ minutes, cool them in iced water and peel.
Bring the stock to a simmer, add the sliced chicken and poach for 6–8 minutes until cooked.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of broth until smooth, then stir it back into the pot without boiling.
Cook the noodles in a separate pan for 3 minutes, adding the halved pak choi for the last minute, and drain.
Divide the noodles and pak choi between bowls, add the chicken, pour over the broth and top with halved eggs and spring onion.
tip: Never boil miso; it loses its flavour.

name: Chicken yogurt sandwich
steps: Shred or chop the cooked chicken.
Mix it with the Greek yogurt, mustard, salt and pepper.
Spread over one slice of bread and add lettuce and cucumber.
Top with the second slice, press down and cut in half.
tip: A healthier take on chicken mayo with twice the protein.

name: Turkey lettuce tacos
steps: Brown the turkey mince in a hot nonstick pan over high heat for 6 minutes, breaking it up.
Add the diced pepper and taco seasoning and cook for 4 minutes with a splash of water.
Separate the lettuce leaves into cups.
Spoon the turkey into the leaves and top with salsa and diced avocado.
Finish with a squeeze of lime.
tip: Add corn tortillas on training days to bring up the carbs.

name: Chicken & pepper paella
ingredients: 1 tsp smoked paprika, a pinch of saffron, lemon
steps: Heat the oil in a wide paella pan or frying pan and brown the chicken pieces for 5 minutes over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and peppers and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the paprika and rice for 1 minute to coat the grains.
Pour in the hot stock with the saffron, spread the rice evenly and simmer without stirring for 18 minutes.
Scatter the peas over, cover with foil and cook for 5 more minutes until the rice is tender.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with lemon wedges.
tip: Do not stir after adding the stock; the crisp base (socarrat) is the best part.

name: Chicken hummus flatbread
steps: Warm the flatbread in a dry pan for 1 minute per side.
Spread the warm flatbread with the hummus right to the edges.
Top with the sliced chicken, rocket and diced tomato.
Roll up or fold in half and eat.
tip: A great way to use leftover roast chicken.

name: Chicken pad Thai
ingredients: 1 tbsp tamarind paste, 1 tsp sugar, lime, spring onions
steps: Soak the rice noodles in hot water for 8 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Mix the tamarind, fish sauce and sugar with 2 tbsp water.
Stir-fry the sliced chicken in the oil in a hot wok for 4–5 minutes until cooked.
Push it aside, scramble the eggs for 1 minute, then add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
Add the beansprouts and toss for 30 seconds more.
Serve topped with chopped peanuts, spring onions and lime.
tip: Have every ingredient ready before you start; it cooks in minutes.

name: Chicken tortilla soup
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chilli powder, lime, coriander
steps: Soften the onion and pepper in a splash of oil in a large pot over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the spices, tomatoes and stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the whole chicken breasts and poach for 15 minutes, then lift out and shred.
Meanwhile cut the tortillas into strips and bake at 200 °C for 8 minutes until crisp.
Return the chicken with the beans and simmer for 3 minutes; season with lime and salt.
Serve topped with tortilla strips and coriander.
tip: Freeze the soup without the tortilla strips.

name: Chicken broccoli pasta bake
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C).
Cook the penne in salted boiling water for 8 minutes, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes, then drain.
Brown the diced chicken in a lightly oiled pan for 6 minutes.
Mix the pasta, broccoli, chicken and passata in a baking dish and season.
Top with torn mozzarella and grated parmesan and bake for 15–20 minutes until bubbling and golden.
tip: Portion into boxes once cool; it keeps 4 days and reheats well.

name: Chicken mango salad
steps: Cook the chicken in a hot pan for 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through, then rest and slice.
Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice and a pinch of chilli for the dressing.
Slice the mango and cucumber.
Toss the leaves, mango, cucumber and mint with the dressing.
Top with the chicken and chopped cashews.
tip: Add 60 g cooked rice noodles to turn it into a recovery meal.

name: Chicken sweetcorn soup
steps: Bring the stock and a slice of ginger to a simmer.
Add the finely diced chicken and sweetcorn and simmer for 8 minutes.
Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp cold water, stir it in and simmer for 1 minute until slightly thickened.
Drizzle in the beaten egg in a thin stream while stirring gently to form ribbons.
Season with tamari and serve topped with spring onions.
tip: Use tamari and cornflour to keep it gluten-free.

name: Salmon rice bowl
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and cook it in 110 ml water in a covered pan: 2 minutes on high, 12 minutes on the lowest heat, then rest for 5 minutes.
Season the salmon and cook it skin-side down in a nonstick pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp, then flip and cook for 2–3 minutes more until it just flakes.
Boil the edamame for 3 minutes and drain.
Slice the cucumber into thin half-moons.
Spoon the rice into a bowl, flake the salmon on top, add the edamame and cucumber, drizzle with soy sauce and finish with sesame and nori.
tip: Use tamari to make it gluten-free; cooked salmon keeps 2 days in the fridge for lunches.

name: Baked salmon & potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C).
Halve the potatoes, toss with half the oil and salt and roast on a lined tray for 15 minutes.
Add the asparagus and the salmon, drizzle with the remaining oil, season and top the salmon with lemon slices.
Roast for 12–14 minutes until the salmon flakes easily and is just opaque in the centre.
Scatter with dill and squeeze over the remaining lemon.
tip: Swap the asparagus for green beans or broccoli outside of asparagus season.

name: Cod Mediterranean traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (fan 190 °C).
Halve the potatoes and roast them with half the oil and salt for 15 minutes.
Add the chopped courgette, pepper, tomatoes and olives, toss with the remaining oil and oregano and roast for 5 minutes more.
Nestle the cod among the vegetables, season and bake for 10–12 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Squeeze lemon over and serve straight from the tray.
tip: Frozen cod fillets work; bake them 5 minutes longer from frozen.

name: Tuna niçoise salad
ingredients: 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp red wine vinegar
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes, adding the egg for the last 8 minutes and the beans for the last 4.
Drain, cool the egg in cold water and peel it.
Whisk the oil, mustard, vinegar and salt into a dressing.
Arrange the leaves, halved potatoes, beans, tomatoes and olives on a plate.
Top with the tuna and quartered egg and drizzle with the dressing.
tip: Pack the dressing separately and it keeps 2 days as a lunch box.

name: Garlic prawn stir-fry
steps: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the packet, then drain and toss with a few drops of oil.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, add the garlic and chilli and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the prawns and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until pink all the way through.
Add the vegetables and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then the noodles and soy sauce and toss for 1 minute.
Serve straight away with lime wedges for squeezing over.
tip: Use tamari to make it gluten-free.

name: Chilli shrimp tacos
ingredients: 1 tsp chilli powder, ½ tsp cumin, coriander
steps: Toss the prawns with the chilli, cumin, salt and a squeeze of lime.
Finely shred the cabbage and toss with lime juice and salt.
Mash the avocado with lime and salt.
Cook the prawns in a hot oiled pan for 2 minutes per side until pink and curled.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill with avocado, cabbage, prawns and coriander; three tacos per person.
tip: Corn tortillas keep these gluten-free.

name: Salmon spinach pasta
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the packet, reserving a cup of the water before draining.
Meanwhile cook the salmon in a nonstick pan over medium heat for 4 minutes per side, then flake it into large pieces.
In the same pan, melt the cream cheese with a little pasta water and the lemon zest into a smooth sauce.
Add the pasta and spinach and toss until the spinach wilts, then fold in the salmon gently.
Season with lemon juice and black pepper.
tip: Hot-smoked salmon flakes straight in and saves cooking time.

name: Kerala fish curry
ingredients: 1 tsp mustard seeds, 10 curry leaves, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli powder
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat, add the mustard seeds and curry leaves and let them pop for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft, then stir in the turmeric and chilli.
Pour in the tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Lay the fish chunks in the sauce, cover and simmer gently for 6–8 minutes until the fish flakes; avoid stirring so it stays in pieces.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, drain and serve with the curry.
tip: Firm fish such as hake, pollock or cod holds together best.

name: Tuna sweetcorn jacket potato
steps: Prick the potato all over with a fork and microwave it on high for 8–10 minutes, turning halfway, until soft in the centre.
For crisp skin, finish it in the oven at 220 °C for 10 minutes.
Mix the tuna, sweetcorn, yogurt, chives and pepper.
Split the potato open, fluff the inside with a fork and pile in the tuna filling.
Serve with the salad leaves on the side.
tip: Bake several potatoes at once; they reheat in 2 minutes.

name: Sardines on toast
steps: Toast the bread until golden and crisp, about 2–3 minutes.
Warm the sardines in their sauce in a small pan for 2 minutes, or use them cold.
Mash them lightly on the toast with a fork.
Squeeze over lemon, add black pepper and serve with sliced tomatoes.
tip: Sardines are among the cheapest sources of omega-3 and calcium (eat the soft bones).

name: Miso-glazed cod
steps: Heat the grill to high and line a tray with foil.
Mix the miso and honey with 1 tsp water and spread it over the top of the cod.
Cook the rice in 320 ml water in a covered pan for 12 minutes and rest for 5.
Grill the cod 10 cm from the heat for 8–10 minutes until caramelised on top and flaking in the centre.
Steam the halved pak choi for 3 minutes.
Serve the cod on rice with the pak choi and spring onions.
tip: White miso is usually gluten-free, but check the label as some contain barley.

name: Smoked mackerel potato salad
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes until tender, then drain and cool.
Mix the yogurt with horseradish, lemon juice and dill.
Slice the potatoes and beetroot and flake the mackerel, removing the skin.
Toss the potatoes with the dressing, then add the rocket, beetroot and mackerel.
tip: Use ready-cooked vacuum-packed beetroot to save time.

name: Seared tuna soba
steps: Cook the soba in boiling water for 4–5 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
Cut the cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks.
Brush the tuna with a little sesame oil, season and sear in a very hot pan for 1 minute per side so it stays pink inside.
Toss the noodles with the soy sauce, remaining sesame oil and vegetables.
Slice the tuna and lay it over the noodles, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tip: For a gluten-free version use 100% buckwheat soba and tamari.

name: Prawn summer rolls
steps: Cook the prawns in boiling water for 2 minutes until pink, cool and halve lengthways.
Soak the noodles in hot water for 3 minutes, drain and cool.
Dip a rice paper sheet in warm water for 10 seconds and lay it on a damp board.
Lay lettuce, noodles, carrot, cucumber, mint and prawns across the lower third, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Whisk the peanut butter with fish sauce, lime and warm water into a dipping sauce.
tip: Cover finished rolls with a damp tea towel so they do not dry out.

name: Hake en papillote
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C) and boil the sliced potatoes for 8 minutes.
Lay a large sheet of baking paper on a tray, put the potatoes, sliced courgette and tomatoes in the centre and place the fish on top.
Add lemon slices, garlic, thyme, the oil and seasoning.
Fold the paper over and crimp the edges tightly to seal the parcel.
Bake for 15–18 minutes and open at the table so the steam escapes.
tip: Works with any white fish; the parcel keeps it moist and saves washing up.

name: Tuna chickpea salad
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Finely chop the red onion and dice the cucumber and tomato.
Toss everything with the oil, lemon juice, parsley and salt.
Flake the tuna over the top.
tip: The flavours improve after an hour, so it is a great make-ahead lunch.

name: Garlic prawns & zoodles
steps: Spiralise the courgettes or cut them into thin ribbons with a peeler.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat, add the garlic and chilli and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes per side until pink.
Add the courgette and tomatoes and toss for 1–2 minutes until just warmed; overcooking makes them watery.
Finish with lemon and parsley.
tip: Add 60 g pasta on training days for more carbs.

name: Oven fish & chips
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (fan 200 °C).
Cut the potatoes into thick chips, toss with the oil and salt and bake for 30 minutes, turning halfway.
Dip the cod in beaten egg and then panko and place on a lined tray.
Bake the fish for the last 15 minutes of the chip time until golden and flaky.
Boil the peas for 3 minutes and crush with a fork.
Serve with lemon wedges and the crushed peas on the side.
tip: Gluten-free breadcrumbs work the same way.

name: Smoked salmon quinoa salad
steps: Simmer the quinoa in 120 ml salted water in a covered pan for 12–15 minutes and fluff.
Let it cool for 5 minutes.
Toss with the rocket, diced cucumber, lemon juice and dill.
Top with the smoked salmon and sliced avocado.
tip: Cook quinoa for the week; it keeps 4 days in the fridge.

name: Tuna poke bowl
steps: Cook the rice in 110 ml water in a covered pan for 12 minutes and rest for 5; season with a splash of rice vinegar.
Cube the tuna and toss it with the soy sauce, sesame oil and chilli; leave for 5 minutes.
Boil the edamame for 3 minutes and drain.
Dice the cucumber and mango.
Arrange everything over the rice and top with spring onion and nori.
tip: Only use fish sold as sashimi-grade; otherwise sear the tuna for 1 minute per side.

name: Mediterranean fish soup
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the sliced onion, fennel and garlic for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the diced potatoes, tomatoes, stock and saffron and simmer for 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the fish in large chunks and the mussels, cover and simmer for 5 minutes until the fish is opaque and the mussels have opened.
Discard any mussels that stay closed and season.
Ladle into deep bowls and scatter with chopped parsley.
tip: Use frozen seafood mix to make it cheaper.

name: Sea bass & herb bulgur
steps: Pour 240 ml boiling salted water over the bulgur, cover and leave for 15 minutes.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes and chop the herbs.
Fluff the bulgur and stir in the vegetables, herbs, half the oil and the lemon juice.
Score the fish skin, season and fry skin-side down in the remaining oil over medium-high heat for 4 minutes until crisp, then flip for 1 minute.
Serve the fish on the bulgur.
tip: Quinoa makes this gluten-free.

name: Salmon potato fishcakes
steps: Boil the peeled potatoes for 15 minutes, drain and mash.
Mix the mash with the flaked salmon, spring onions, dill, lemon zest and seasoning, then shape into 8 cakes.
Dip each cake in beaten egg, then panko.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and hot through.
Serve two cakes per person with salad.
tip: Freeze uncooked cakes on a tray, then bag; fry from frozen for 6 minutes per side.

name: Prawn coconut curry
steps: Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Soften the onion in a splash of oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink, then stir in the spinach until wilted.
Season and serve over the rice.
tip: Frozen prawns can go straight in; add 2 minutes to the cooking time.

name: Tuna pasta salad
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the packet, drain and rinse under cold water.
Drain the tuna and halve the tomatoes.
Toss the pasta with the oil, lemon juice and salt.
Fold in the tuna, sweetcorn, tomatoes and basil.
tip: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; a perfect post-gym box.

name: Beef chili con carne
ingredients: 2 tsp chilli powder, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp oregano, 2 garlic cloves
steps: Brown the mince in a large pot over high heat for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains; pour off any fat.
Add the onion, pepper and garlic and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spices and tomato purée for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes, beans and 150 ml water.
Simmer uncovered on low for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and rich.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Season the chili and serve a quarter over a quarter of the rice.
tip: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months; a square of dark chocolate deepens the flavour.

name: Lean spaghetti bolognese
ingredients: 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 bay leaf
steps: Cook the onion, carrot and celery in a splash of oil in a large pan over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and sweet.
Turn up the heat, add the mince and garlic and brown for 6 minutes, breaking it up.
Pour in the passata, add the oregano and bay leaf and simmer gently, partly covered, for 25–30 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted water according to the packet and drain, reserving a little water.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and a splash of pasta water and serve with grated parmesan.
tip: The sauce freezes perfectly; make a double batch.

name: Beef & broccoli stir-fry
steps: Cook the rice in 320 ml water in a covered pan for 12 minutes and rest for 5.
Slice the steak very thinly against the grain and toss with the cornflour and half the soy sauce.
Stir-fry the beef in half the oil in a very hot wok for 2 minutes until browned; set aside.
Add the remaining oil, garlic, ginger and broccoli with 3 tbsp water and stir-fry for 4 minutes until just tender.
Return the beef with the oyster sauce and remaining soy and toss for 1 minute until glossy.
Spoon over the rice and serve straight away.
tip: Partly freezing the steak for 20 minutes makes it much easier to slice thinly.

name: Steak & sweet potato
ingredients: 1 garlic clove, chilli, red wine vinegar
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (fan 200 °C), cut the sweet potato into wedges and roast for 25–30 minutes.
Take the steak out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking and season well.
Chop the herbs with the garlic, chilli, oil and vinegar for a quick chimichurri.
Sear the steak in a smoking-hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side for medium-rare, then rest it for 5 minutes.
Boil the beans for 4 minutes, slice the steak and serve with the wedges and chimichurri.
tip: Resting the steak keeps the juices in; slice against the grain.

name: Light beef stroganoff
steps: Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Slice the beef into thin strips and sear it in a hot lightly oiled pan for 2 minutes in batches; set aside.
Fry the onion and mushrooms for 6 minutes until golden, then stir in the paprika.
Lower the heat, stir in the crème fraîche, mustard and a splash of water and simmer for 2 minutes.
Return the beef just to warm through, season and serve over the rice with parsley.
tip: Do not boil the sauce once the beef is back in, or the meat turns tough.

name: Beef soft tacos
steps: Brown the mince in a hot pan over high heat for 6 minutes, breaking it up.
Add the taco seasoning and 4 tbsp water and simmer for 3 minutes until saucy.
Shred the cabbage finely and toss with lime juice and salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds per side.
Fill each with beef, cabbage, salsa and sliced avocado; three per person.
tip: Corn tortillas keep it gluten-free; check your taco seasoning too.

name: Thai beef noodle salad
steps: Soak the noodles in hot water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
Sear the steak in a smoking-hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side, then rest for 5 minutes and slice thinly.
Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and chilli into a dressing.
Cut the cucumber and carrot into ribbons with a peeler.
Toss the noodles, vegetables, herbs and dressing, then top with the beef.
tip: Keeps for a day in the fridge; add the herbs fresh before eating.

name: Beef ragout with polenta
ingredients: 2 bay leaves, thyme, 1 tbsp flour or cornflour
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (fan 140 °C).
Brown the beef in the oil in a casserole over high heat in two batches, 4 minutes each, and set aside.
Fry the onion, carrots and mushrooms for 6 minutes, then return the beef with the tomatoes, stock, bay and thyme.
Cover and cook in the oven for 1 hour 45 minutes until the beef is tender enough to cut with a spoon.
Shortly before serving, whisk the polenta into 800 ml boiling salted water and cook for 5–10 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Serve the ragout over the soft polenta.
tip: Even better the next day; freezes well for 3 months.

name: Lean beef burger
steps: Season the mince with salt and pepper and shape into two patties slightly wider than the buns, pressing a dimple in the centre.
Cook in a hot pan or on a grill over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side for medium.
Toast the buns cut-side down for 1 minute.
Build the burgers with mustard, lettuce, tomato, onion, gherkins and the patty.
tip: Add oven wedges on training days for a complete recovery meal.

name: Beef & lentil cottage pie
steps: Boil the peeled potatoes for 15 minutes, drain and mash with the milk and seasoning.
Brown the mince in a large pan for 6 minutes, then add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato purée, stock and lentils and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C), spoon the filling into a baking dish and spread the mash on top.
Rough up the surface with a fork and bake for 25 minutes until golden.
tip: The lentils stretch the meat, cut cost and add fibre.

name: Korean beef bulgogi bowl
ingredients: 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 tsp sesame seeds, chilli flakes
steps: Cook the rice in 320 ml water in a covered pan for 12 minutes and rest for 5.
Mix the soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic and ginger.
Brown the mince in a hot pan over high heat for 6 minutes until crisp in places.
Pour in the sauce and cook for 2 minutes until sticky.
Serve over the rice with the julienned carrot and cucumber, sesame seeds and chilli flakes.
tip: Use tamari to make it gluten-free.

name: Roast beef sandwich
steps: Spread the bread with horseradish or mustard.
Layer the roast beef over one slice.
Add rocket and sliced tomato and season.
Top with the second slice and cut in half.
tip: Leftover home-roasted beef is leaner and cheaper than deli slices.

name: Beef pho
ingredients: 1 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 slices ginger, 1 onion halved, lime, chilli
steps: Char the onion halves and ginger in a dry pan for 4 minutes, then add to the stock with the spices.
Simmer the stock for 15 minutes, then strain and season with fish sauce.
Slice the steak paper-thin; partly freezing it for 20 minutes helps.
Cook the noodles according to the packet and divide between bowls with the raw beef and beansprouts.
Ladle the boiling broth over; it cooks the beef in about 30 seconds.
Add herbs, lime and chilli to taste.
tip: The broth must be at a full boil to cook the beef safely.

name: Beef goulash soup
ingredients: 2 tbsp sweet paprika, 1 tsp caraway seeds, 2 garlic cloves
steps: Brown the diced beef in the oil in a large pot over high heat for 6 minutes.
Add the sliced onions and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the paprika and caraway (paprika burns easily), then add the tomatoes and stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the diced potatoes and peppers and simmer for 25 minutes more until the beef is tender.
Season and serve in deep bowls.
tip: Freezes well; a spoon of yogurt on top is traditional.

name: Steak & quinoa salad
steps: Simmer the quinoa in 120 ml salted water in a covered pan for 12–15 minutes and fluff.
Sear the seasoned steak in a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side, then rest for 5 minutes and slice.
Dice the pepper and halve the tomatoes.
Toss the quinoa, rocket and vegetables with the oil and balsamic.
Top with the sliced steak.
tip: Cook the steak the night before and slice it cold for a lunch box.

name: Pork tenderloin & apples
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C).
Boil the halved potatoes for 10 minutes, then drain.
Brown the seasoned pork on all sides in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 5 minutes.
Add the apple wedges, onion and potatoes around it with the thyme and roast for 18–20 minutes until the pork reaches 63 °C in the centre.
Rest the pork for 5 minutes, boil the beans for 4 minutes and slice the pork to serve.
tip: Pork tenderloin is as lean as chicken breast and cooks fast.

name: Ginger pork stir-fry
steps: Cook the rice in 320 ml water in a covered pan for 12 minutes and rest for 5.
Slice the pork thinly and toss with half the soy sauce and the grated ginger.
