Stir-fry the pork in the oil in a very hot wok for 3–4 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the pepper and pak choi and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the remaining soy sauce, toss for 30 seconds and serve over the rice.
tip: Tamari keeps it gluten-free.

name: Pulled pork carnitas bowl
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp oregano, 3 garlic cloves, lime
steps: Rub the pork with cumin, oregano, salt and garlic and put it in a slow cooker or casserole with the onion and orange juice.
Cook on low for 4 hours (or at 150 °C in the oven, covered) until it falls apart.
Shred the pork with two forks, then spread it on a tray and grill for 5 minutes until the edges crisp.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and warm the beans.
Serve each bowl with rice, beans, pork, salsa and lime.
tip: Freeze the shredded pork in portions with some of the cooking juices.

name: Baked pork schnitzel
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (fan 200 °C) and boil the potatoes for 20 minutes.
Flatten the pork steaks to 5 mm between cling film with a rolling pin.
Dip them in beaten egg, then panko, place on a lined tray and drizzle with the oil.
Bake for 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Slice the cucumber thinly and mix with yogurt, dill and salt.
Serve with the potatoes, cucumber salad and lemon wedges.
tip: Turkey or chicken escalopes work exactly the same way.

name: Lamb kofta & couscous
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp ground coriander, 1 garlic clove
steps: Mix the lamb with the spices, garlic, half the herbs and salt and shape into 8 sausage-shaped kofta.
Cook under a hot grill or in a griddle pan for 10–12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Pour 225 ml boiling salted water over the couscous, cover for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes and mix with the remaining herbs.
Serve the kofta on the couscous with the salad and tzatziki.
tip: Shape the kofta the night before; they hold together better when chilled.

name: Lamb & apricot tagine
ingredients: 2 tsp ras el hanout, 1 cinnamon stick, coriander
steps: Brown the diced lamb in a splash of oil in a casserole over high heat for 6 minutes.
Add the onion and ras el hanout and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, cinnamon and 300 ml water, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and apricots and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Pour 360 ml boiling water over the couscous, cover for 5 minutes and fluff.
Serve the tagine over the couscous with coriander.
tip: Use rice or quinoa instead of couscous for a gluten-free version.

name: Lamb steak & bean salad
steps: Season the lamb steak and cook it in a hot pan for 3–4 minutes per side for pink, then rest for 5 minutes.
Boil the green beans for 4 minutes and drain.
Toss the white beans, green beans and chopped tomato with the oil, lemon juice and mint.
Slice the lamb and lay it over the salad.
tip: Leftover roast lamb makes this a 5-minute lunch.

name: Shepherd's pie
ingredients: 1 tbsp tomato purée, a few sprigs of thyme
steps: Boil the peeled potatoes for 15 minutes, drain and mash with the milk.
Brown the lamb in a large pan over high heat for 6 minutes and pour off excess fat.
Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes, then the stock and thyme and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the peas, spoon into a baking dish and cover with the mash.
Bake at 200 °C (fan 180 °C) for 25 minutes until golden.
tip: Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies; leave it out for fish allergies.

name: Red lentil dal
ingredients: 2 garlic cloves, 1 thumb ginger, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp garam masala
steps: Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat, add the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then the onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and garam masala for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and 600 ml water and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils collapse into a thick purée.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Stir the spinach into the dal until wilted, season with salt and lemon and serve over the rice.
tip: Freezes in portions for 3 months; one of the cheapest high-fibre meals you can make.

name: Chickpea spinach curry
ingredients: 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp garam masala
steps: Put the brown rice on to cook in plenty of salted water for 25 minutes, then drain.
Fry the onion in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes, add the garlic and spices and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas, crush a few chickpeas with the spoon to thicken the sauce and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted and season.
Spoon over the rice and serve straight away.
tip: Add 200 g cubed tofu with the chickpeas for an extra 10 g protein per serving.

name: Teriyaki tofu bowl
steps: Press the tofu between kitchen paper for 10 minutes, cut into cubes and toss with the cornflour.
Cook the rice in 160 ml water in a covered pan for 12 minutes and rest for 5.
Fry the tofu in a lightly oiled nonstick pan over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides.
Add the teriyaki sauce and toss for 1 minute until sticky.
Steam the broccoli and edamame for 4 minutes.
Serve everything over the rice and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tip: Use a gluten-free teriyaki or tamari-based sauce if you avoid gluten.

name: Sweet potato & bean tacos
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, lime, coriander
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (fan 200 °C).
Dice the sweet potato into 1.5 cm cubes, toss with the spices, salt and a little oil and roast for 20–25 minutes until soft and caramelised.
Warm the black beans with a splash of water and lightly crush them.
Shred the cabbage and toss with lime juice.
Warm the tortillas and fill with beans, sweet potato, cabbage, avocado, salsa and coriander; three per person.
tip: The roasted sweet potato keeps 4 days and works in bowls and salads too.

name: Tempeh veg stir-fry
steps: Cook the brown rice in plenty of boiling water for 25 minutes and drain (or use pre-cooked rice).
Slice the tempeh into thin strips and steam or simmer it for 5 minutes to soften its bitterness.
Fry the tempeh in the oil in a hot wok for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and vegetables and stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and maple syrup and toss for 1 minute until glossy, then serve over the rice.
tip: Tamari makes this gluten-free.

name: Peanut tofu noodles
ingredients: 1 lime, 1 tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp maple syrup
steps: Press the tofu for 10 minutes, cube it and fry in a lightly oiled pan over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until golden.
Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the packet and drain.
Whisk the peanut butter, tamari, lime juice, chilli, maple syrup and 5 tbsp hot water into a smooth sauce.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, julienned carrot and beansprouts over low heat for 1 minute.
Top with the tofu and extra lime.
tip: The sauce keeps a week in a jar and is great on salads too.

name: Three-bean vegan chili
ingredients: 2 tsp chilli powder, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 2 garlic cloves
steps: Soften the onion, peppers and garlic in the oil in a large pot over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Stir in the spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, rinsed lentils, all the beans and 300 ml water.
Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have dissolved into a thick sauce.
Season and serve with rice, corn tortillas or a baked potato.
tip: The red lentils add protein and make the chili thick without any meat.

name: Baked falafel wrap
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 garlic clove, 2 tbsp flour, lemon
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C).
Pulse the drained chickpeas with the herbs, garlic, cumin, flour and salt into a coarse paste.
Shape into 10 small patties, place on a lined tray, spray with oil and bake for 20–25 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp.
Thin the tahini with lemon juice and water into a drizzling sauce.
Fill each wrap with lettuce, tomato, falafel and tahini sauce and roll up.
tip: Baked falafel freeze well; reheat at 200 °C for 10 minutes.

name: Lentil bolognese
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, rinsed lentils, passata and 500 ml water.
Simmer partly covered for 25–30 minutes until the lentils are tender, adding water if needed.
Cook the spaghetti according to the packet and drain.
Season the sauce with oregano and basil and serve over the pasta.
tip: Use lentil or gluten-free pasta to make it gluten-free.

name: Vegan Buddha bowl
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (fan 190 °C), toss the cubed sweet potato and chickpeas with paprika and a little oil and roast for 25 minutes.
Simmer the quinoa in 240 ml salted water in a covered pan for 15 minutes and fluff.
Massage the kale with a pinch of salt and lemon for 1 minute until it softens.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice and water into a dressing.
Build the bowls with quinoa, kale, sweet potato and chickpeas and drizzle with dressing.
tip: Roast a double tray of chickpeas and sweet potato for the week.

name: Miso tofu udon soup
steps: Bring 400 ml water to a simmer and add the cubed tofu and halved pak choi for 3 minutes.
Add the udon and heat for 2 minutes, loosening the noodles with chopsticks.
Take the pan off the heat, dissolve the miso in a ladle of broth and stir it back in.
Pour into a deep bowl and top with spring onion, nori and chilli.
tip: Never boil miso; adding it off the heat keeps its flavour.

name: Seitan gyros pita
ingredients: 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp paprika, 1 garlic clove, lemon
steps: Slice the seitan thinly and toss with the oil, oregano, paprika and salt.
Fry in a hot pan over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Mix the soy yogurt with grated garlic, lemon and salt for a vegan tzatziki.
Warm the pitas, then fill with seitan, tomato, onion and the sauce.
tip: Seitan is pure wheat gluten, so it is not suitable for coeliacs.

name: Red lentil pasta arrabbiata
steps: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, add the garlic and chilli and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt and simmer for 10 minutes.
Cook the lentil pasta in salted water for the time on the packet, usually 7–8 minutes, and drain.
Stir the spinach into the sauce, then toss with the pasta and basil.
tip: Lentil pasta is naturally gluten-free and has twice the protein of wheat pasta.

name: Tofu banh mi
steps: Toss the julienned carrot with a splash of rice vinegar, a pinch of sugar and salt and leave for 10 minutes.
Slice the tofu and fry it in a dry nonstick pan for 3 minutes per side, then splash with soy sauce.
Warm the baguette in the oven for 3 minutes until crisp.
Fill with the tofu, pickled carrot, cucumber, coriander and chilli.
tip: The quick pickles keep a week in the fridge.

name: Quinoa tabbouleh with beans
ingredients: a big bunch of parsley and mint
steps: Simmer the quinoa in 240 ml salted water in a covered pan for 15 minutes, then spread on a plate to cool.
Finely chop the herbs and dice the tomatoes and cucumber.
Whisk the oil and lemon juice with salt.
Toss everything with the quinoa and beans.
tip: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and is gluten-free, unlike classic bulgur tabbouleh.

name: Smoked tofu potato hash
steps: Dice the potatoes and microwave them in a covered bowl for 5 minutes.
Fry them in the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat for 10 minutes until crisp.
Add the diced tofu, onion and pepper and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Stir in the sauerkraut and caraway for 2 minutes and season.
tip: A hearty, high-protein vegan brunch; add a fried egg if you eat eggs.

name: Vegan recovery shake
steps: Pour the soy drink into the blender first.
Add the pea protein, banana, oats and maple syrup.
Blend for 45 seconds until smooth and creamy.
Drink within 30 minutes after training.
tip: Freeze banana chunks for a thicker, colder shake.

name: Tofu tikka wraps
steps: Press the tofu for 10 minutes and cut into thick sticks.
Mix half the soy yogurt with the tikka spice and lemon, coat the tofu and marinate for 10 minutes.
Bake at 220 °C (fan 200 °C) on a lined tray for 18–20 minutes until charred at the edges.
Mix the remaining yogurt with chopped mint and grated cucumber for raita.
Warm the wraps, fill with cabbage, tofu and raita and roll up.
tip: The marinated tofu keeps 3 days and works cold in salads.

name: Black bean quinoa bowl
steps: Simmer the quinoa in 140 ml salted water with a pinch of cumin for 15 minutes and fluff.
Warm the beans and sweetcorn together for 3 minutes.
Dice the tomato and avocado.
Build the bowl with quinoa, beans and corn, tomato, avocado and salsa and finish with lime and coriander.
tip: A complete vegan protein; keeps 3 days without the avocado.

name: Mushroom stroganoff
steps: Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Fry the sliced mushrooms in the oil over high heat for 6 minutes until browned, then add the onion for 4 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, beans and 100 ml water and simmer for 3 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the soy yogurt and mustard and season.
Serve over the rice with parsley.
tip: Adding the yogurt off the heat stops it from splitting.

name: Halloumi veg traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (fan 190 °C).
Toss the potatoes, peppers, courgette, onion and chickpeas with the oil, oregano and salt on a large tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once.
Lay the sliced halloumi on top and roast for 10 more minutes until golden.
Squeeze over lemon and serve.
tip: Halloumi is salty, so go easy on salt for the vegetables.

name: Veggie lentil lasagne
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (fan 170 °C).
Grate the courgettes and cook them in a pan for 5 minutes, then add the lentils, passata, garlic and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season the ricotta and loosen it with a few tablespoons of water.
Layer sauce, lasagne sheets and ricotta three times in a large dish, finishing with sauce.
Top with mozzarella and parmesan, cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover for 15 minutes until golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into 6 portions.
tip: Freeze portions individually; reheat covered at 180 °C for 30 minutes.

name: Älplermagronen
steps: Peel and dice the potatoes and cook them with the pasta in salted water for the time on the pasta packet, then drain.
Meanwhile slowly fry the sliced onions in the butter over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until golden and sweet.
Return the pasta and potatoes to the pot with the milk and cheese and stir over low heat for 2 minutes until creamy.
Serve topped with the onions and applesauce on the side.
tip: The Alpine classic: the tart applesauce cuts through the cheese.

name: Palak paneer (light)
ingredients: ginger, garlic, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp cumin
steps: Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Wilt the spinach in a pan with a splash of water, then blend to a purée.
Fry the onion with ginger, garlic and spices in a splash of oil for 6 minutes, add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach purée and cubed paneer and simmer for 5 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the yogurt and serve with the rice.
tip: Frozen spinach works perfectly and needs no wilting.

name: Spanish potato tortilla
steps: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes and onion.
Cook them gently in the oil in a 24 cm nonstick pan over low heat, covered, for 20 minutes until soft but not browned.
Beat the eggs with salt, add the potatoes and rest for 5 minutes.
Pour back into the pan and cook on low for 6 minutes until almost set.
Flip using a plate and cook for 3 more minutes, then cool slightly and cut into quarters.
tip: Eat it cold the next day; it travels perfectly.

name: Vegetable egg fried rice
steps: Use cooked and cooled rice from the day before.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the vegetables for 2 minutes.
Push them aside, scramble the eggs for 1 minute, then add the rice.
Toss for 3–4 minutes until piping hot, then add the soy sauce and spring onions.
tip: Add 150 g edamame for a bigger protein hit.

name: Mushroom parmesan risotto
steps: Fry the mushrooms in a splash of oil over high heat for 6 minutes until golden; set aside.
Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, then add the rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, waiting until each is absorbed, for about 18 minutes.
Stir in the peas, mushrooms and parmesan for the last 2 minutes.
Rest for 1 minute so it turns creamy, then serve.
tip: Stir in 150 g white beans for extra protein without changing the texture.

name: Bean & cheese quesadilla
steps: Mash the beans roughly with a fork.
Spread them over half the tortilla, top with cheese and sweetcorn and fold over.
Cook in a dry pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and the cheese melts.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa.
tip: Use a corn tortilla for a gluten-free version.

name: Creamy cottage cheese pasta
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the packet.
Blend the cottage cheese with garlic and a splash of pasta water into a smooth sauce.
Drain the pasta and toss it with the sauce, spinach and halved tomatoes over low heat for 1 minute.
Serve topped with parmesan and chilli flakes.
tip: Blending cottage cheese gives a creamy sauce with 18 g protein and almost no fat.

name: Lentil & feta salad
steps: Drain and rinse the lentils if canned.
Dice the pepper and cucumber and finely slice the onion.
Toss with the oil, lemon juice, parsley and salt.
Crumble the feta over the top just before serving.
tip: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; perfect for lunch boxes.

name: Halloumi couscous bowl
steps: Pour 105 ml boiling salted water over the couscous, cover for 5 minutes and fluff.
Fry the sliced halloumi in a dry nonstick pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Dice the tomato and cucumber and mix with the couscous, chickpeas and lemon juice.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the hot halloumi slices.
tip: Quinoa makes it gluten-free.

name: Bean & egg skillet
steps: Simmer the tomatoes, beans, garlic and paprika in a small pan for 6 minutes until thick.
Stir in the spinach, then make two wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook on low for 5–6 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve with the toasted bread.
tip: Use gluten-free bread or skip it to make it gluten-free.

name: Greek salad protein bowl
steps: Cook the quinoa in 80 ml salted water for 15 minutes in advance, or use pre-cooked quinoa.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes.
Toss with the chickpeas, olives, quinoa, oil, oregano and salt.
Crumble the feta over the top just before serving.
tip: Keeps 2 days in a box; add the feta just before eating.
